text:
Denver Barkey was a 95th overall pick in 2023, the kind of player teams hope becomes a useful NHLer someday. At 21, he's already one for the Flyers. His two goals against Columbus on Nov. 14, including the winner, were his first multi-goal game in the league and gave Philadelphia its first divisional win of the season.

He has 11 points in 20 games, seven in his last ten, and five on the power play. The scoring is running a little hot (four goals on 2.96 expected, a 20% shooting rate on just 20 shots), so don't expect the goals to keep this pace. What looks real is everything else. Philadelphia takes 55% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice and is almost 13 points worse without him, one of the biggest gaps on the team. Evolving-Hockey liked his defense last season too: opponents' chances dropped with him out there, 91st percentile among forwards.

Flyers reporter Charlie O'Connor singled out a shift by Barkey and Christian Dvorak this week, two players battling for every loose puck. That's his game: small details, done every shift.
headline: Barkey, the third-rounder, keeps earning minutes
